feedback: Evidence: iteration 0 (span ±0.024 m, 12 mm) scored 54.37 with one line loss per run and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 1 (span ±0.03 m, 12 mm) scored 69.32, so widening the span helped, but line loss stayed at about 1 per run (1.65 on oval). Steering_oscillation stayed around 0.14 in both, so the failure is abrupt loss of the tape, not jitter. The 16 mm footprint you have proposed is a sound next step for that failure. I have not measured its result, and I make no claim about it here. Your off-track limit arithmetic is correct: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) is 0.06 m for any body width in your range, so body_width is not a lever. If the 16 mm race reduces line_loss_events and raises progress, keep the 16 mm footprint and test the span next. Iteration 0 to 1 showed that a 0.006 m span increase gave +15 points, so a wider span is the natural follow-up. If line loss persists at about 1 per run with 16 mm, the footprint is not the cause. In that case, hold the geometry and consider a forward offset test as a separate change.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events falls with sensor_size 0.016, keep it and test a wider span of about ±0.04 m (sensor x at -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04), a continuation of the trend from ±0.024 to ±0.03 m that raised the score from 54.37 to 69.32.
If line_loss_events stays near 1 per run with sensor_size 0.016, hold the geometry and test a forward offset of about 0.03 m as the only change, to check whether sensor timing at bends is the limit.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 at speed after any change, reduce the forward offset rather than widening the span further, because the span has so far only been tested alongside controller changes.
